Table marts.property_yield — Gross rental yield by (postcode, property_type, month) — sales JOIN rent, the combined view neither single-source mart can answer, at the same month grain as property_sales and property_rent. Physical table: marts.property_yield. Ported from docs/chronicle/property_yield_20241003.py. Keeps the additive components (total_sale_value, n_sold, total_weekly_rent, n_rented) so a consumer re-aggregating to quarter, year, SA3 or across property types can recompute averages and yield; gross_yield_pct is a derived ratio-of-averages (52 * avg_weekly_rent / avg_sale_price * 100), not an average of per-row yields. Thin cells are floored per month at n_sold >= 5 and n_rented >= 5. Belongs to the `nsw_yield` dataset (its own RLS grant). Verified by assert_property_yield_has_coverage and assert_property_yield_range.
Columns:
  postcode — Postcode. Join key to dim_postcode_geo for region rollups.
  property_type — 'house' or 'unit', standardised the same way as the sales/rent marts.
  month — Calendar month (first-of-month date) both sales and rent were aggregated to. Part of the grain.
  total_sale_value — Additive sum of sale_price (AUD) for the cell. Use with n_sold to re-aggregate avg_sale_price.
  n_sold — Additive count of sales in the cell (>= 5 by construction).
  total_weekly_rent — Additive sum of weekly_rent (AUD) for the cell. Use with n_rented to re-aggregate avg_weekly_rent.
  n_rented — Additive count of bonds in the cell (>= 5 by construction).
  avg_sale_price — Cell-level average sale price. Re-aggregate from sum(total_sale_value)/sum(n_sold), not by averaging this.
  avg_weekly_rent — Cell-level average weekly rent. Re-aggregate from sum(total_weekly_rent)/sum(n_rented), not by averaging this.
  gross_yield_pct — Gross rental yield %: 52 * avg_weekly_rent / avg_sale_price * 100. A derived ratio-of-averages — for a rollup, recompute it from the summed components, don't average these.
